title: Creative revision
summary: Build, encounter failure, and revise your approach as the constraints change.
intro: A fictional shelter-design exercise using a tarp, rope, five sticks, duct tape, and a garbage bag. Each step follows your choices. These are possible consequences, not predictions or a creativity score. No real shelter is being built or tested.

questions.prompt: How would you begin your shelter design?

options.label: Sketch a supported frame before assembling anything
Build a small prototype and see what happens
Look at examples of shelters with similar materials
Ask a partner to design it with me

questions.scenario: The practice site is dry and sheltered. You have time to explore.

questions.prompt: Your first prototype collapses under a test load. What do you do next?

options.label: Change one joint and test it again
Start again with a different structure
Ask someone to help locate the weak point
Compare your structure with a worked example

variants.text: You followed your sketch. In this simulation, a joint twisted even though the overall frame looked balanced.
Your quick prototype exposed a twisting joint before you used all the materials.
Your example used rigid poles; these flexible sticks twisted at a joint.
You and your partner had different assumptions about how to brace the joint. It twisted under load.

questions.prompt: The same joint loosens again. You learn that the tape does not adhere well to the tarp. What now?

options.label: Replace the taped joint with a rope fastening and compare
Design a structure that does not depend on that joint
Test the available materials separately before rebuilding
Ask your partner to propose another fastening

variants.text: Your local repair lasted longer, but it still loosened. The new material information changes what is worth testing.
Your new structure reused the same taped fastening, and it also loosened.
Your helper isolated the fastening as the weak point. A material test now explains why.
The worked example assumed waterproof tape. Your available tape behaves differently.

questions.prompt: One stick breaks and your available build time is halved. What would you preserve?

options.label: Reduce the design to one small covered area
Reuse the sound parts and alter the supports
Split the remaining work with a partner
Try a different low structure with fewer supports

questions.scenario: There is no real emergency. This is a new constraint in the design exercise.

questions.prompt: Your revised model stands. How would you check it?

options.label: Apply the same small test load and compare
Test the part most likely to fail next
Ask someone who has not seen it to review it
Build two small variants to compare

questions.prompt: You discover that the shelter is for keeping equipment dry, not for people to sit inside. What changes?

options.label: Keep the design if it already meets that need
Lower the cover and remove unnecessary space
Ask how much equipment and what weather it must handle
Compare the present design with a smaller alternative

questions.scenario: This new information changes the design goal, not your worth as a designer.

questions.prompt: Which next step would best explain your revision process?

options.label: Record what changed and the evidence behind it
Show the sequence of prototypes to someone
Try the same constraints with another design goal
List what is still unknown and ask for feedback

questions.scenario: Use the optional note to explain why you kept or changed your approach. There is no single correct path.
